correctness.rationale: For each oriented vertex-edge incidence on a path, gradient membership is equivalent to explicit unary constraints on the comparison directions of at most two adjacent path edges. Every consistent comparison assignment comes from a strict vertex ordering because a path is acyclic. Thus forbidden incidence pairs are exhaustive; orbit barycenters triangulate the actual involution fixed space, and only the last left-oriented orbit is removed. The surviving orbit conflicts are precisely consecutive edges and odd-to-next-plus-three edges of the stated finite graph. A leaf-neighbor decomposition is the union of two cones along the independence complex of a remaining graph explicitly isomorphic to the graph at index m-2. The two base complexes yield the all-parameter homotopy classification. The extracted standalone verifier checks 409112 original-order instances, 797157 ternary word instances, graph isomorphisms up to m=30 and independent exact finite homology through m=7. Finite computations corroborate but do not replace the symbolic argument.
